title.zh: 卷九十八 志第五十一 禮一
title.raw: 卷九十八 志第五十一 禮一 Volume 98 Treatises 51: Rites 1

sentences.zh: 吉禮一

translations.literal: Felicitous Rites I.
translations.idiomatic: Felicitous Rites (Part One).

sentences.zh: 太宗尚儒雅，勤於治政，修明典章，大抵曠廢舉矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong honored refined learning, was diligent in governing affairs, clarified institutions and ordinances, and for the most part revived what had long lain abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong favored scholarly refinement and threw himself into administration, clarifying institutions and ordinances and largely reviving practices that had fallen into disuse.

sentences.zh: 真宗承重熙之後，契丹既通好，天下無事，於是封泰山，祀汾陰，天書、聖祖崇奉迭興，專置詳定所，命執政、翰林、禮官參領之。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong succeeded after the Chongxi era; once peace was made with the Khitan and the realm was untroubled, he performed the feng on Mount Tai and sacrificed at Fenyin; cults to the Heavenly Writ and the Sacred Ancestor rose one after another; a dedicated office for detailed review was established, and chief ministers, Hanlin scholars, and ritual officers were ordered to take part in leading it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong came to the throne after the Chongxi era. With peace made with the Khitan and the empire untroubled, he mounted the feng rites on Mount Tai and sacrificed at Fenyin; cults to the Heavenly Writ and the Sacred Ancestor followed one upon another. A dedicated office for detailed review was set up, and chief ministers, Hanlin scholars, and ritual officers were charged to oversee it.

sentences.zh: 尋改禮儀院，仍歲增修，纖微委曲，緣情稱宜，蓋一時彌文之制也。

translations.literal: Soon it was renamed the Court of Ritual; each year it was further revised, with minute detail shaped to circumstance as propriety required—altogether the ornate ceremonial code of the age.
translations.idiomatic: It was soon retitled the Court of Ritual, revised annually with ever finer detail, shaped to circumstance as propriety required—the ornate ceremonial code of the times.

sentences.zh: 自《通禮》之後，其制度儀注傳於有司者，殆數百篇。

translations.literal: After the Comprehensive Rites, the regulations and ritual protocols held by the responsible agencies numbered nearly three hundred separate works.
translations.idiomatic: Following the Comprehensive Rites, the regulations and ritual protocols held by the responsible agencies ran to nearly three hundred separate works.

sentences.zh: 先是，天禧中，陳寬編次禮院所承新舊詔敕，不就。

translations.literal: Previously, during Tianxi, Chen Kuan arranged the ritual office's old and new edicts but did not finish.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, during Tianxi, Chen Kuan had begun arranging old and new edicts held by the ritual office, but never finished.

sentences.zh: 天聖初，王皞始類成書，盡乾興，為《禮閣新編》，大率禮文，無著述體，而本末完具，有司便之。

translations.literal: In early Tiansheng, Wang Hao first classified and completed a book through the Qianxing reign as the New Compilation of the Ritual Archive; it was mostly ritual text without the form of a formal treatise, yet beginning and end were complete, which the agencies found convenient.
translations.idiomatic: In early Tiansheng, Wang Hao first assembled a classified compilation through the Qianxing reign, called New Compilation of the Ritual Archive. It was mostly ritual text without the structure of a formal treatise, yet covered everything start to finish, which the agencies found practical.

sentences.zh: 景祐四年，賈昌朝撰《太常新禮》及《祀儀》，止于慶曆三年。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingyou, Jia Changchao compiled the Court of Imperial Sacrifices New Rites and Sacrificial Protocols, stopping at the third year of Qingli.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyou 4, Jia Changchao drafted the Court of Imperial Sacrifices New Rites and Sacrificial Protocols, carrying through Qingli 3.

sentences.zh: 皇祐中，文彥博又撰《大享明堂記》二十卷。

translations.literal: During Huangyou, Wen Yanbo also compiled the Record of the Grand Offering at the Bright Hall in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: During Huangyou, Wen Yanbo likewise wrote the Record of the Grand Offering at the Bright Hall in twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 至嘉祐中，歐陽修纂集散失，命官設局，主《通禮》而記其變，及《新禮》以類相從，為一百卷，賜名《太常因革禮》，異于舊者蓋十三四焉。

translations.literal: By Jiayou, Ouyang Xiu collected and collated what had been scattered and lost, had officials set up an office, took the Comprehensive Rites as the main text while noting changes, and grouped the New Rites by category into one hundred juan, granted the title Rites of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Through Reform; what differed from the old was roughly thirteen or fourteen parts in ten.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiayou, Ouyang Xiu collected and collated scattered material, had an office set up, used the Comprehensive Rites as the backbone while noting alterations, and grouped the New Rites by category into one hundred juan, entitled Rites of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Through Reform—roughly thirteen or fourteen percent unlike the older version.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又命龍圖直學士宋敏求同御史台、閣門、禮院詳定《朝會儀注》，總四十六卷：曰《閣門儀》，曰《朝會禮文》，曰《儀注》，曰《徽號寶冊儀》。

translations.literal: Before long, Dragon Diagram Academician-in-Attendance Song Minqiu was also ordered, together with the Censorate, Gate Office, and ritual court, to fix the Protocols for Court Assemblies, forty-six juan in all: Gate Office Protocols, Court Assembly Ritual Texts, Protocol Directions, and Protocols for Honorific Titles and Imperial Registers.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Song Minqiu, Dragon Diagram Academician-in-Attendance, was joined with the Censorate, Gate Office, and ritual court to fix the Protocols for Court Assemblies—forty-six juan in all: Gate Office Protocols, Court Assembly Ritual Texts, Protocol Directions, and Protocols for Honorific Titles and Imperial Registers.

sentences.zh: 《祭祀》總百九十一卷：曰《祀儀》，曰《南郊式》，曰《大禮式》，曰《郊廟奉祀禮文》，曰《明堂袷享令式》，曰《天興殿儀》，曰《四孟朝獻儀》，曰《景靈宮供奉敕令格式》，曰《儀禮敕令格式》。

translations.literal: Under Sacrifice, one hundred ninety-one juan in all: Sacrificial Protocols, Southern Suburb Forms, Great Rite Forms, Suburban and Temple Sacrificial Ritual Texts, Bright Hall Joint Offering Command Forms, Hall of Heavenly Prosperity Protocols, Four Seasonal Morning Offering Protocols, Hall of Numinous Splendor Supply Edicts and Formats, and Ritual Edicts and Formats.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sacrifice came 191 juan: Sacrificial Protocols, Southern Suburb Forms, Great Rite Forms, Suburban and Temple Sacrificial Ritual Texts, Bright Hall Joint Offering Command Forms, Hall of Heavenly Prosperity Protocols, Four Seasonal Morning Offering Protocols, Hall of Numinous Splendor Supply Edicts and Formats, and Ritual Edicts and Formats.

sentences.zh: 《祈禳》總四十卷：曰《祀賽式》，曰《齋醮式》，曰《金籙儀》。

translations.literal: Prayer and Exorcism, forty juan in all: Sacrificial Competition Forms, Purification and Offering Forms, and Golden Register Protocols.
translations.idiomatic: Prayer and Exorcism comprised forty juan: Sacrificial Competition Forms, Purification and Offering Forms, and Golden Register Protocols.

sentences.zh: 《蕃國》總七十一卷：曰《大遼令式》，曰《高麗入貢儀》，曰《女真排辦儀》，曰《諸蕃進貢令式》。

translations.literal: Foreign States, seventy-one juan in all: Liao Command Forms, Koryŏ Tribute-Entry Protocols, Jurchen Arrangement Protocols, and Various Barbarian Tribute-Entry Command Forms.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign States ran to seventy-one juan: Liao Command Forms, Koryŏ Tribute-Entry Protocols, Jurchen Arrangement Protocols, and Various Barbarian Tribute-Entry Command Forms.

sentences.zh: 《喪葬》總百六十三卷：曰《葬式》，曰《宗室外臣葬敕令格式》，曰《孝贈式》。

translations.literal: Mourning and Burial, one hundred sixty-three juan in all: Burial Forms, Imperial Clan and Outer Official Burial Edicts and Formats, and Filial Gift Forms.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning and Burial totaled 163 juan: Burial Forms, Imperial Clan and Outer Official Burial Edicts and Formats, and Filial Gift Forms.

sentences.zh: 其損益之制，視前多矣。

translations.literal: Provisions for what to add or cut were far more numerous than before.
translations.idiomatic: Provisions for what to add or cut were vastly more than in earlier compilations.

sentences.zh: 紹聖而後，累詔續編，起治平，訖政和，凡五十一年，為書三百卷，今皆不傳。

translations.literal: After Shaosheng, edicts repeatedly called for continued compilation from Zhiping through Zhenghe—fifty-one years in all, yielding three hundred juan, none of which survives today.
translations.idiomatic: From Shaosheng onward, edicts repeatedly called for further compilation from Zhiping to Zhenghe—fifty-one years in all, yielding three hundred juan, all now lost.

sentences.zh: 而大觀初，置議禮局於尚書省，命詳議、檢討官具禮制本末，議定請旨。

translations.literal: At the opening of Daguan, a Bureau for Discussion of Rites was placed in the Ministry of Revenue, with deliberation and collation officers to set out each rite from beginning to end, decide it, and seek imperial approval.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Daguan, a Bureau for Discussion of Rites was placed in the Ministry of Revenue, with deliberation and collation officers to trace each rite from origin to end, settle it, and seek imperial confirmation.

sentences.zh: 三年書成，為《吉禮》二百三十一卷、《祭服制度》十六卷，頒焉。

translations.literal: Three years later the work was finished as Auspicious Rites in two hundred thirty-one juan and Regulations for Sacrificial Garments in sixteen juan, and was promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later the work was finished: Auspicious Rites in 231 juan and Regulations for Sacrificial Garments in 16 juan, then issued.

sentences.zh: 議禮局請分秩五禮，詔依《開寶通禮》之序。

translations.literal: The bureau requested that the Five Rites be ranked in order; an edict directed that the sequence follow the Kaibao Comprehensive Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The bureau asked that the Five Rites be ranked and ordered; the throne directed that the sequence follow the Kaibao Comprehensive Rites.

sentences.zh: 政和元年，續修成四百七十七卷，且命仿是修定儀注。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenghe the continued edition reached four hundred seventy-seven juan, and orders were given to use it as the model for revising ritual protocols.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenghe 1 the continued edition reached 477 juan, with orders to use it as the model for revising ritual protocols.

sentences.zh: 三年，《五禮新儀》成，凡二百二十卷，增置禮直官，許士庶就問新儀，而詔開封尹王革編類通行者，刊本給天下，使悉知禮意，其不奉行者論罪。

translations.literal: In the third year the New Protocols of the Five Rites were completed—two hundred twenty juan in all; ritual duty officers were added, scholars and commoners were allowed to inquire about the new protocols, and the Director of Kaifeng Wang Ge was ordered to compile what could be put into practice, print copies for the empire, make ritual meaning known, and punish failure to comply.
translations.idiomatic: In year three the New Protocols of the Five Rites appeared—220 juan—with new ritual duty officers and leave for scholars and commoners to inquire about them. Wang Ge, Director of Kaifeng, was told to compile what could be put into practice, print copies for the empire, and make ritual meaning known; failure to comply was criminal.

sentences.zh: 宣和初，有言其煩擾者，遂罷之。

translations.literal: Early in Xuanhe, critics said it was burdensome, and it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xuanhe, critics called it unwieldy, and the project was dropped.

sentences.zh: 初，議禮局之置也，詔求天下古器，更制尊、爵、鼎、彝之屬。

translations.literal: When the bureau was first established, an edict sought ancient vessels throughout the realm and had new sets of zun, jue, ding, and yi made.
translations.idiomatic: When the bureau was first set up, the court solicited ancient vessels nationwide and had new sets of zun, jue, ding, and yi made.

sentences.zh: 其後，又置禮制局於編類御筆所。

translations.literal: Later a Bureau for Ritual Systems was also placed at the office that compiled the emperor's draft writings.
translations.idiomatic: Later a Bureau for Ritual Systems was added to the office that compiled the emperor's draft writings.

sentences.zh: 於是郊廟禋祀之器，多更其舊。

translations.literal: Thereupon many implements used in suburban and temple offerings were changed from their former types.
translations.idiomatic: Many implements used in suburban and temple offerings were then altered from their former types.

sentences.zh: 既有詔討論冠服，遂廢靴用履，其他無所改議，而禮制局亦罷。

translations.literal: An edict then called for discussion of caps and dress; boots were abandoned in favor of shoes, but nothing else was changed in debate, and the Bureau for Ritual Systems was also abolished.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then called for review of caps and dress; boots gave way to shoes, but little else was changed before that bureau too was shut down.

sentences.zh: 大抵累朝典禮，講議最詳。

translations.literal: On the whole, successive dynasties' canonical ceremonies were debated with the greatest thoroughness.
translations.idiomatic: On the whole, successive courts debated canonical ceremony with unusual thoroughness.

sentences.zh: 祀禮修于元豐，而成於元祐，至崇寧復有所增損。

translations.literal: Sacrificial rites were revised in Yuanfeng, completed in Yuanyou, and in Chongning were again increased or reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial rites were reworked under Yuanfeng, finished under Yuanyou, and revised again in Chongning.

sentences.zh: 其存於有司者，惟《元豐郊廟禮文》及《政和五禮新儀》而已。

translations.literal: What remained with the agencies were only the Yuanfeng Suburban and Temple Ritual Texts and the Zhenghe New Protocols of the Five Rites.
translations.idiomatic: What the agencies still held were the Yuanfeng Suburban and Temple Ritual Texts and the Zhenghe New Protocols of the Five Rites alone.

sentences.zh: 乃若圜丘之罷合祭天地；

translations.literal: Such as ending the combined sacrifice of Heaven and Earth at the Round Mound;
translations.idiomatic: Such as ending the combined sacrifice of Heaven and Earth at the Round Mound;

sentences.zh: 明堂專以英宗配帝，悉罷從祀群神；

translations.literal: at the Bright Hall pairing only Emperor Yingzong with the Thearch and ending all collateral spirit offerings;
translations.idiomatic: at the Bright Hall pairing only Emperor Yingzong with the Thearch and ending all collateral spirit offerings;

sentences.zh: 大蠟分四郊；

translations.literal: splitting the great la sacrifice among the four suburbs;
translations.idiomatic: splitting the great la sacrifice among the four suburbs;

sentences.zh: 壽星改祀老人；

translations.literal: replacing the Longevity Star rite with worship of the Old Man;
translations.idiomatic: replacing the Longevity Star rite with worship of the Old Man;

sentences.zh: 禧祖已祧而復，遂為始祖；

translations.literal: Ancestor Xi, who had been displaced, was restored and made founding ancestor;
translations.idiomatic: restoring Ancestor Xi, who had been displaced, as founding ancestor;

sentences.zh: 即景靈宮建諸神禦殿，以四孟薦享；

translations.literal: spirit halls were built at the Hall of Numinous Splendor for seasonal offerings;
translations.idiomatic: building spirit halls at the Hall of Numinous Splendor for seasonal offerings;

sentences.zh: 虛禘祭；

translations.literal: the di and xia sacrifices were hollowed out;
translations.idiomatic: hollowing out the di and xia sacrifices;

sentences.zh: 去牙盤食；

translations.literal: tray-and-stand food was done away with;
translations.idiomatic: doing away with tray-and-stand food;

sentences.zh: 卻尊號；

translations.literal: honorific titles were declined;
translations.idiomatic: declining honorific titles;

sentences.zh: 罷入閣儀並常朝及正衙橫行。

translations.literal: entry into the privy chamber, regular audiences, and cross-processions at the main court were canceled.
translations.idiomatic: and canceling entry into the privy chamber, regular audiences, and cross-processions at the main court—

sentences.zh: 此熙甯、元豐變禮之最大者也。

translations.literal: These were the greatest ritual changes of the Xining and Yuanfeng periods.
translations.idiomatic: these were the largest ritual reforms of the Xining and Yuanfeng periods.

sentences.zh: 元祐冊後，政和冠皇子，元符創景靈西宮，崇甯親祀方澤、作明堂、立九廟、鑄九鼎、祀熒惑，大觀受八寶、大祀皆前期十日而戒。

translations.literal: Later came enfeoffing the empress in Yuanyou, crowning an imperial prince in Zhenghe, the western Hall of Numinous Splendor in Yuanfu, Chongning's personal sacrifices at the Square Mound, Bright Hall rites, Nine Temples, Nine Cauldrons, and rites to the Sparkling Deluder; Daguan's reception of the Eight Treasures; and ten-day warnings before every great sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Later came enfeoffing the empress in Yuanyou, crowning an imperial prince in Zhenghe, the western Hall of Numinous Splendor in Yuanfu, Chongning's personal sacrifices at the Square Mound, Bright Hall rites, Nine Temples, Nine Cauldrons, and rites to the Sparkling Deluder; Daguan's reception of the Eight Treasures; and ten-day warnings before every great sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 凡此蓋治平以前所未嘗行者。

translations.literal: None of this had been done before Zhiping.
translations.idiomatic: None of this had been done before Zhiping.

sentences.zh: 欽宗即位，嘗詔春秋釋奠改從《元豐儀》，罷《新儀》不用而未暇也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Qinzong took the throne, he once ordered spring and autumn shidian to follow Yuanfeng forms and the New Protocols set aside, but there was no time to carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: On accession, Emperor Qinzong ordered spring and autumn shidian to follow Yuanfeng forms and the New Protocols set aside, but the court never had time to implement it.

sentences.zh: 靖康之厄，蕩析無餘。

translations.literal: The disaster of Jingkang left nothing standing.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingkang disaster left nothing standing.

sentences.zh: 南渡中興，銳意修復，高宗嘗謂輔臣曰：「晉武平吳之後，上下不知有禮，旋致禍亂。

translations.literal: After crossing south and rebuilding, the court was keen to restore rites; Emperor Gaozong once told his ministers: "After Jin Wu pacified Wu, court and country forgot ceremony, and ruin followed quickly.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing south and rebuilding, the court worked hard to restore rites. Emperor Gaozong told his ministers: "When Jin Wu pacified Wu, court and country forgot ceremony, and ruin followed quickly.

sentences.zh: 周禮不秉，其何能國？

translations.literal: Without holding to the rites of Zhou, how can there be a state?
translations.idiomatic: Without the rites of Zhou, how can a state endure?

sentences.zh: 」孝宗繼志，典章文物，有可稱述。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong carried on that aim; in statutes and ritual objects there was much worth noting.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong carried on that aim; in statutes and ritual objects there was much worth noting.

sentences.zh: 治平日久，經學大明，諸儒如王普、董{分廾}等多以禮名家。

translations.literal: In a long age of peace, classical studies flourished, and scholars such as Wang Pu and Dong [fen gong] among others made names in ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In a long age of peace, classical studies revived, and scholars like Wang Pu and Dong [fen gong] among others made names in ritual.

sentences.zh: 當時嘗續編《太常因革禮》矣，淳熙復有編輯之旨。

translations.literal: The court then continued the Rites Through Reform; in Chunxi there was again an editorial mandate.
translations.idiomatic: The court then continued the Rites Through Reform; Chunxi brought another editorial mandate.

sentences.zh: 其後朱熹講明詳備，嘗欲取《儀禮》、《周官》、《二戴記》為本，編次朝廷公卿大夫士民之禮，盡取漢、晉而下及唐諸儒之說，考訂辨正，以為當代之典，未及成書而沒。

translations.literal: Later Zhu Xi lectured with great completeness and wished to take the Ceremonies, the Offices of Zhou, and the two Dai ritual records as the foundation, ordering rites for court, nobles, officials, and people, drawing on Han through Tang commentators to correct and fix practice for the present—he died before finishing the book.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi later lectured with great completeness and planned to base a code on the Ceremonies, Offices of Zhou, and the two Dai ritual records, ordering rites for court, nobles, officials, and people, drawing on Han through Tang commentators to correct and fix practice for the present—he died before finishing.

sentences.zh: 理宗四十年間，屢有意乎禮文之事，雖曰崇尚理學，所謂「禮雲禮雲，玉帛雲乎哉」，蓋可三歎。

translations.literal: Across Emperor Lizong's forty years the throne often turned to ritual texts; though Neo-Confucian learning was prized, one may thrice sigh at the saying "Rites, rites—is it only jade and silk?"
translations.idiomatic: Across Emperor Lizong's forty years the throne often turned to ritual texts; though Neo-Confucian learning was prized, one may thrice sigh at the question whether rites are only jade and silk.

sentences.zh: 鹹淳以降，無足言者。

translations.literal: After Xianchun there is little worth mentioning.
translations.idiomatic: After Xianchun there is little to record.

sentences.zh: 今因前史之舊，芟其繁亂，匯為五禮，以備一代之制，使後之觀者有足征焉。

translations.literal: Here, following earlier histories, we prune the tangled and assemble the Five Rites to preserve the institutions of the age, so later readers have adequate evidence.
translations.idiomatic: Here, following earlier histories, we prune the tangled and assemble the Five Rites so the institutions of the age remain on record for later readers.

sentences.zh: 五禮之序，以吉禮為首，主邦國神祇祭祀之事。

translations.literal: In the order of the Five Rites, felicitous rites stand first, governing sacrifice to the state's spirits and gods.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Five Rites, felicitous rites stand first, governing sacrifice to state and land spirits.

sentences.zh: 凡祀典皆領于太常。

translations.literal: Every entry in the sacrificial canon is overseen by the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Every entry in the sacrificial canon falls under the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 歲之大祀三十：正月上辛祈谷，孟夏雩祀，季秋大享明堂，冬至圜丘祭昊天上帝，正月上辛又祀感生帝，四立及土王日祀五方帝，春分朝日，秋分夕月，東西太一，臘日大蠟祭百神，夏至祭皇地祇，孟冬祭神州地祇，四孟、季冬薦享太廟、後廟，春秋二仲及臘日祭太社、太稷，二仲九宮貴神。

translations.literal: Thirty great sacrifices fill the year: first-month shang day prayer for grain; midsummer rain rite; autumn's last month and winter solstice offerings to Heaven at the Round Mound; first-month shang day to the Life-Giving Spirit; four establishments and earth-king days to the Five Thearchs; equinox audience with sun and moon; eastern and western Grand Unity; la day great la to the hundred spirits; summer solstice to Earth; early winter to the Spirit of the Divine State's land; four seasonal months and winter's last month at Grand and Rear Temples; spring and autumn mid-months and la day to Grand Earth and Grain altars; mid-season rites to the nine-palace noble spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty great sacrifices fill the year: first-month shang day prayer for grain; midsummer rain rite; autumn's last month and winter solstice offerings to Heaven at the Round Mound; first-month shang day to the Life-Giving Spirit; four establishments and earth-king days to the Five Thearchs; equinox audience with sun and moon; eastern and western Grand Unity; la day great la to the hundred spirits; summer solstice to Earth; early winter to the Spirit of the Divine State's land; four seasonal months and winter's last month at Grand and Rear Temples; spring and autumn mid-months and la day to Grand Earth and Grain altars; mid-season rites to the nine-palace noble spirits.

sentences.zh: 中祀九：仲春祭五龍，立春後醜日祀風師、亥日享先農，季春巳日享先蠶，立夏後申日祀雨師，春秋二仲上丁釋奠文宣王、上戊釋奠武成王。

translations.literal: Nine medium sacrifices: mid-spring to the Five Dragons; post-spring-establishment chou day to the Wind Master and hai day to the Former Farmer; last spring si day to the Former Silkworm; post-summer-establishment shen day to the Rain Master; spring and autumn upper ding shidian to the Cultural Thearch and upper wu to the Martial Completion King.
translations.idiomatic: Nine medium sacrifices: mid-spring to the Five Dragons; post-spring-establishment chou day to the Wind Master and hai day to the Former Farmer; last spring si day to the Former Silkworm; post-summer-establishment shen day to the Rain Master; spring and autumn upper ding shidian to the Cultural Thearch and upper wu to the Martial Completion King.

sentences.zh: 小祀九：仲春祀馬祖，仲夏享先牧，仲秋祭馬社，仲冬祭馬步，季夏土王日祀中霤，立秋後辰日祀靈星，秋分享壽星，立冬後亥日祠司中、司命、司人、司祿，孟冬祭司寒。

translations.literal: Nine minor sacrifices: mid-spring Horse Ancestor; midsummer Former Herdsman; mid-autumn Horse Altar; midwinter Horse Pace; last summer earth-king day Central Drain; post-autumn chen day Numinous Star; autumn Longevity Star; post-winter hai day to the four Directors; early winter Spirit of Cold.
translations.idiomatic: Nine minor sacrifices: mid-spring Horse Ancestor; midsummer Former Herdsman; mid-autumn Horse Altar; midwinter Horse Pace; last summer earth-king day Central Drain; post-autumn chen day Numinous Star; autumn Longevity Star; post-winter hai day to the four Directors; early winter Spirit of Cold.

sentences.zh: 其諸州奉祀，則五郊迎氣日祭嶽、鎮、海、瀆，春秋二仲享先代帝王及週六廟，並如中祀。

translations.literal: For prefectural sacrifices, on the five-suburb qi-reception days mountains, seas, and streams are sacrificed to; in spring and autumn mid-months former dynasties' rulers and Zhou's six temples are enjoyed—all as medium rites.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural sacrifices follow the same ranks: five-suburb qi-reception days to mountains, seas, and streams; spring and autumn mid-months to former dynasties' rulers and Zhou's six temples—as medium rites.

sentences.zh: 州縣祭社稷，奠文宣王，祀風雨，並如小祀。

translations.literal: Counties sacrifice to local soil-and-grain altars, shidian to the Cultural Thearch, and wind and rain—all as minor rites.
translations.idiomatic: Counties sacrifice to local soil-and-grain altars, shidian to the Cultural Thearch, and wind and rain—as minor rites.

sentences.zh: 凡有大赦，則令諸州祭嶽、瀆、名山、大川在境內者，及歷代帝王、忠臣、烈士載祀典者，仍禁近祠廟鹹加祭。

translations.literal: Whenever there is a great amnesty, prefectures are ordered to sacrifice to mountains, rivers, and famous streams within their borders and to successive rulers, loyal ministers, and martyrs entered in the sacrificial canon, while excessive offerings at nearby shrines are forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: On great amnesties, prefectures must sacrifice to local mountains, rivers, and canonized rulers and martyrs, but may not pile extra rites on nearby shrines.

sentences.zh: 有不克定時日者，太卜署預擇一季祠祭之日，謂之「畫日」。

translations.literal: When a fixed date cannot be settled, the Directorate of Divination pre-selects a seasonal sacrifice day in advance—called the "painted day."
translations.idiomatic: If no fixed date is possible, the Directorate of Divination chooses a seasonal sacrifice day in advance—the "painted day."

sentences.zh: 凡壇壝、牲器、玉帛、饌具、齋戒之制，皆具《通禮》。

translations.literal: Rules for altars, victims, vessels, jade, offerings, and purification are all set out in the Comprehensive Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Altars, victims, vessels, jade, offerings, and purification rules all appear in the Comprehensive Rites.

sentences.zh: 後復有高禖、大小酺神之屬，增大祀為四十二焉。

translations.literal: Later high qi and great and small exorcism spirits were added, raising great sacrifices to forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Later high qi and great and small exorcism spirits were added, raising great sacrifices to forty-two.

sentences.zh: 其後，神宗詔改定大祀：太一，東以春，西以秋，中以夏冬；

translations.literal: Later Emperor Shenzong ordered great sacrifices revised: Grand Unity east in spring, west in autumn, center in summer and winter;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong then ordered great sacrifices revised: Grand Unity east in spring, west in autumn, center in summer and winter;

sentences.zh: 增大蠟為四，東西蠟主日配月；

translations.literal: the great la was expanded to four, eastern and western la pairing sun with moon;
translations.idiomatic: great la expanded to four, eastern and western la pairing sun with moon;

sentences.zh: 太廟月祭朔。

translations.literal: Grand Temple offering on each month's first day.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Temple offering on each month's first day.

sentences.zh: 而中祀：四望，南北蠟。

translations.literal: Medium sacrifices added the Four Outlooks and northern and southern la.
translations.idiomatic: Medium sacrifices added the Four Outlooks and northern and southern la.

sentences.zh: 小祀：以四立祭司命、戶、灶、中霤、門、厲、行，以藏冰、出冰祭司寒，及月薦新太廟。

translations.literal: Minor sacrifices: at the four establishments to fate, household, stove, central drain, gate, pestilence, and travel spirits; at ice storage and removal to Cold; monthly new grain at the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Minor sacrifices: at four establishments to fate, household, stove, central drain, gate, pestilence, and travel spirits; at ice storage and removal to Cold; monthly new grain at the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 歲通舊祀凡九十二，惟五享後廟焉。

translations.literal: Annual rites under the old count totaled ninety-two, apart from five Rear Temple offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Annual rites under the old count totaled ninety-two, apart from five Rear Temple offerings.

sentences.zh: 政和中，定《五禮新儀》，以熒惑、陽德觀、帝鼐、坊州朝獻聖祖、應天府祀大火為大祀；

translations.literal: In Zhenghe the New Protocols of the Five Rites fixed the Sparkling Deluder, Yang Virtue Hall, Emperor Nai, Fengzhou Sacred Ancestor morning offering, and Yingtianfu Great Fire rites as great sacrifices;
translations.idiomatic: Zhenghe's New Protocols made the Sparkling Deluder, Yang Virtue Hall, Emperor Nai, Fengzhou Sacred Ancestor morning offering, and Yingtianfu Great Fire rites great sacrifices;

sentences.zh: 雷神、歷代帝王、寶鼎、牡鼎、蒼鼎、岡鼎、彤鼎、阜鼎、皛鼎、魁鼎、會應廟、慶厲軍祭後土為中祀；

translations.literal: Thunder Spirit, successive rulers, precious cauldrons and the nine tripods, Responsive Assembly Temple, and Qingli army earth rite as medium sacrifices;
translations.idiomatic: Thunder Spirit, successive rulers, precious cauldrons and the nine tripods, Responsive Assembly Temple, and Qingli army earth rite as medium sacrifices;

sentences.zh: 山林川澤之屬，州縣祭社稷、祀風伯雨師雷神為小祀。

translations.literal: mountains, rivers, and marshes, plus local soil-and-grain and wind-rain-thunder rites, as minor sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: mountains, rivers, and marshes, plus local soil-and-grain and wind-rain-thunder rites, as minor sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 餘悉如故。

translations.literal: Everything else remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else stayed as before.

sentences.zh: 建炎四年十一月，權工部尚書韓肖胄言：「祖宗以來，每歲大、中、小祀百有餘所，罔敢廢闕。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year of Jianyan, Acting Works Minister Han Xiaozhou memorialized: "Since the founders, each year the court has observed well over a hundred great, medium, and minor sacrifices without fail.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan 4.11, Acting Works Minister Han Xiaozhou memorialized: "Since the founders, the court has observed well over a hundred great, medium, and minor sacrifices yearly without fail.

sentences.zh: 自車駕巡幸，惟存宗廟之祭，至天地諸神之祀，則廢而不舉。

translations.literal: Since the imperial carriage went on tour, only ancestral temple rites remain; sacrifices to Heaven, Earth, and the other spirits have been abandoned and are not performed.
translations.idiomatic: Since the flight south, only ancestral temple rites continue; Heaven, Earth, and the spirit hosts go unhonored.

sentences.zh: 今國步尚艱，天未悔禍，正宜齋明恭肅，通於神明，而忽大事、棄重禮，恐非所以消弭天災，導迎景貺。

translations.literal: The realm is still in peril and Heaven has not turned from calamity—precisely when we should be pure and solemn before the spirits, yet we neglect the greatest duties and abandon weighty rites; I fear this is not the way to quiet disaster and draw down blessing.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is still in peril and Heaven has not turned from calamity—precisely when we should be pure and solemn before the spirits, yet we neglect the greatest duties and heaviest rites; that may not be how to quiet disaster and draw blessing.

sentences.zh: 雖小祀未可遍舉，如天地、五帝、日月星辰、社稷，欲詔有司以時舉行。

translations.literal: Although minor rites cannot all be restored, for Heaven and Earth, the Five Thearchs, sun, moon, stars, and the soil-and-grain altars, I ask that the agencies be ordered to perform them on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Not every minor rite can be restored, but for Heaven and Earth, the Five Thearchs, sun, moon, stars, and the soil-and-grain altars, let the agencies hold them on schedule.

sentences.zh: 所有器服並牲牢禮料，恐國用未充，難如舊制，乞下太常寺相度裁定，省繁就簡，庶幾神不乏祀，仰副陛下昭事懷柔、為民求福之意。

translations.literal: Vessels, dress, victims, and ritual supplies may exceed what the state treasury can supply and may not match the old scale; I ask that the Court of Imperial Sacrifices measure and fix them, simplifying where the old scale is impossible, so spirits are not left hungry and Your Majesty's intent—to serve Heaven clearly and seek the people's good—may still be met.
translations.idiomatic: Vessels, dress, victims, and supplies may exceed present means; let the Court of Imperial Sacrifices simplify where the old scale is impossible, so spirits are not left hungry and Your Majesty's intent—to serve Heaven clearly and seek the people's good—may still be met.

sentences.zh: 」尋命禮部太常裁定：每歲以立春上辛祀谷，孟夏雩祀，季秋及冬至日四祀天，夏至日一祀地，立春上辛日祀感生帝，立冬後祀神州地祇，春秋二社及臘前一日祭太社、太稷。

translations.literal: Soon the Ministry of Rites and Court of Imperial Sacrifices fixed the calendar: spring's first shang day for grain; midsummer rain; autumn's last month and winter solstice for Heaven (four times); summer solstice for Earth; spring's first shang for Life-Giving Spirit; after winter establishment for the Divine State's land spirit; spring and autumn she days and the eve of la for Grand Earth and Grain.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites and Court of Imperial Sacrifices then fixed the calendar: spring's first shang day for grain; midsummer rain; autumn's last month and winter solstice for Heaven (four times); summer solstice for Earth; spring's first shang for Life-Giving Spirit; after winter establishment for the Divine State's land spirit; spring and autumn she days and the eve of la for Grand Earth and Grain.

sentences.zh: 免牲、玉，權用酒酺，仍依方色奠幣。

translations.literal: Victims and jade were set aside; wine libations stood in temporarily, with silks still by directional color.
translations.idiomatic: Victims and jade were set aside; wine libations stood in temporarily, with silks still by directional color.

sentences.zh: 以輔臣為初獻，禮官為亞、終獻。

translations.literal: Chief ministers made the primary offering; ritual officers the secondary and final.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers made the primary offering; ritual officers the secondary and final.

sentences.zh: 紹興三年，復大火祀，配以閼伯，以辰、戌出納之月祀之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shaoxing the Great Fire rite was restored, with Quebo as associate, sacrificed in the chen and xu months of its rising and setting.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxing 3 restored the Great Fire rite with Quebo as associate, in the chen and xu months of its rising and setting.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，禮部太常寺言：「每歲大祀三十六，除天地、宗廟、社稷、感生帝、九宮貴神、高禖、文宣王等已行外，其餘並乞寓祠齋宮。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year the Ministry of Rites and Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported: "Each year thirty-six great sacrifices remain; aside from Heaven and Earth, temples, soil and grain, Life-Giving Spirit, nine-palace spirits, high qi, Cultural Thearch, and the like already performed, the rest are all requested as lodged rites at the purification palace.
translations.idiomatic: In year 27 they reported: "Thirty-six great sacrifices yearly remain; aside from those already held—to Heaven and Earth, temples, soil and grain, Life-Giving Spirit, nine-palace spirits, high qi, Cultural Thearch, and the like—let the rest be performed as lodged rites at the purification palace.

sentences.zh: 」自紹興以來，大祀所行二十有三而已，至是乃悉復之。

translations.literal: Since Shaoxing only twenty-three great rites had been performed; now the full set was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Since Shaoxing only twenty-three great rites had been held; now the full set returned.

sentences.zh: 舊制，郊廟祝文稱嗣皇帝，諸祭稱皇帝。

translations.literal: Formerly suburban and temple prayers named the heir emperor; other sacrifices said emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly suburban and temple prayers named the heir emperor; other sacrifices said emperor.

sentences.zh: 著作局准《開元禮》全稱帝號。

translations.literal: The Composition Office, following the Kaiyuan Rites, used the full imperial title.
translations.idiomatic: The Composition Office, following the Kaiyuan Rites, used the full imperial title.

sentences.zh: 真宗以兼秘書監李至請，改從舊制。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong, on Li Zhi's request as concurrent Secretariat Director, reverted to the older form.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong, on Li Zhi's request as concurrent Secretariat Director, reverted to the older form.

sentences.zh: 又諸祭祝辭皆臨事撰進，多違典禮，乃命至增撰舊辭八十四首，為《正辭錄》三卷。

translations.literal: Prayers for every sacrifice had been drafted on the spot, often breaking precedent; Li Zhi was told to add eighty-four standard prayers in three juan, the Correct Prayer Record.
translations.idiomatic: Prayers for every sacrifice had been drafted on the spot, often breaking precedent; Li Zhi was told to add eighty-four standard prayers in three juan, the Correct Prayer Record.

sentences.zh: 既復命知制誥李宗諤、楊億、直史館陳彭年詳定之，以為永式。

translations.literal: Drafting controllers Li Zong'e and Yang Yi and Academician Chen Pengnian were then assigned to fix them as permanent forms.
translations.idiomatic: Drafting controllers Li Zong'e and Yang Yi and Academician Chen Pengnian were then assigned to fix them as permanent forms.

sentences.zh: 祝版當進署者，並命秘閣吏書，上親署訖，禦寶封給之。

translations.literal: Prayer boards needing signature were copied by Secretariat clerks; the emperor signed them, sealed them, and issued them.
translations.idiomatic: Prayer boards needing signature were copied by Secretariat clerks; the emperor signed them, sealed them, and issued them.

sentences.zh: 凡先代帝王，祝文止稱廟號。

translations.literal: Prayers to former dynasties' rulers used temple names only.
translations.idiomatic: Prayers to former dynasties' rulers used temple names only.

sentences.zh: 凡親行大祀，則皇子弟為亞獻、終獻。

translations.literal: When the emperor led a great sacrifice in person, imperial clansmen were secondary and final offerers.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor led a great sacrifice in person, imperial clansmen were secondary and final offerers.

sentences.zh: 五代以來，宰相為大禮使，太常卿為禮儀使，御史中丞為儀仗使，兵部尚書為鹵簿使，京府尹為橋道頓遞使。

translations.literal: Since the Five Dynasties, the chief minister headed the Grand Ritual Commission, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices director the Ritual Protocol Commission, the vice censor-in-chief the Protocol of Honor Commission, the war minister the Halberd Array Commission, and the capital intendant the Bridge and Relay Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Five Dynasties, the chief minister headed the Grand Ritual Commission, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices director the Ritual Protocol Commission, the vice censor-in-chief the Protocol of Honor Commission, the war minister the Halberd Array Commission, and the capital intendant the Bridge and Relay Commission.

sentences.zh: 至是，大禮使或用親王，禮儀使專命翰林學士，儀仗、鹵簿使亦或以他官。

translations.literal: By then the grand ritual role might fall to a prince; ritual protocol went to Hanlin scholars; honor and halberd posts might go to others.
translations.idiomatic: By then the grand ritual role might fall to a prince; ritual protocol went to Hanlin scholars; honor and halberd posts might go to others.

sentences.zh: 太平興國九年，始鑄五使印。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taiping Xingguo seals were first cast for the five commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping Xingguo 9 first cast seals for the five commissioners.

sentences.zh: 太宗將封泰山，以儀仗使兼判橋道頓遞事。

translations.literal: As Emperor Taizong prepared the Mount Tai feng, the Protocol of Honor Commissioner also judged bridge and relay affairs.
translations.idiomatic: As Emperor Taizong prepared the Mount Tai feng, the Protocol of Honor Commissioner also judged bridge and relay affairs.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符後，凡有大禮，以中書、樞密分為五使，仍特鑄印。

translations.literal: After Dazhong Xiangfu, whenever there was a great rite the Secretariat and Military Affairs were split into five commissions, each with its own seal.
translations.idiomatic: After Dazhong Xiangfu, every great rite split the Secretariat and Military Affairs into five commissions, each with its own seal.

sentences.zh: 景祐二年，詔有司：「皇地祇、神州，舊常參官攝事，非所以尊神，自今命兩省。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingyou, an edict told the agencies: "Earth and the Divine State's land spirit were long served by routine officials acting as proxies—not fit honor for the gods. Hereafter the two departments shall be charged.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingyou 2 the throne told the agencies: "Earth and the Divine State's land spirit were long served by routine officials acting as proxies—not fit honor for the gods. Hereafter the two departments shall be charged.

sentences.zh: 歲九大祠，宰臣攝事者，參知政事、尚書丞郎、學士奉祠。

translations.literal: Each year at the nine great sacrifices, when chief ministers stood in to conduct affairs, Vice Grand Councilors, section directors and deputies of the Masters of Writing, and academicians performed the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Each year at the nine great sacrifices, when chief ministers served as proxies, Vice Grand Councilors, Masters of Writing section chiefs and deputies, and Hanlin academicians carried out the offerings.

sentences.zh: 」於是參知政事盛度，享太廟已受誓戒，除知樞密院，乃不奉祠。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon Vice Grand Councilor Sheng Du, having already received the abstention vows for the Grand Ancestral Temple offering, was appointed to head the Bureau of Military Affairs and therefore did not perform the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: ” Vice Grand Councilor Sheng Du had already taken the abstention vows for the Grand Ancestral Temple rite when he was transferred to head Military Affairs—so he never performed the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 又故事，三歲一親郊，不郊輒代以他禮，慶賞與郊同，而五使皆以輔臣，不以官之高下。

translations.literal: By precedent, every three years the emperor personally performed the suburban sacrifice; when no suburban rite was held, another ritual replaced it, rewards and enfeoffments matching the suburban rite; the five commissioners were always chief ministers, without regard to rank.
translations.idiomatic: By old custom the emperor went out to the suburbs every three years; if the suburban rite was skipped, another ceremony stood in, with rewards and enfeoffments on the suburban scale. The five commissioners were always grand councilors, rank notwithstanding.

sentences.zh: 天聖中，乃以朝林學士領儀仗，御史中丞領鹵簿，始用官次。

translations.literal: In the Tiansheng era, a Hanlin academician was made to lead the protocol of honor and the vice censor-in-chief the halberd array—the first time official rank order was used.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tiansheng, a Hanlin academician first took the honor commission and the vice censor-in-chief the halberd array—rank order replacing ministerial standing.

sentences.zh: 又每歲大祀，皆遣台省近臣攝太尉，其後或委他官，太中祥符始復舊制。

translations.literal: Also, each year at the great sacrifices, a censorate or secretariat intimate was dispatched to stand in as Grand Marshal; later the duty was sometimes assigned to other officials; only in the Taizong-Xiangfu era was the old system restored.
translations.idiomatic: Each great annual sacrifice also sent a censorate or secretariat intimate to serve as Grand Marshal; later others sometimes took the post, until Taizong’s Xiangfu reign restored the old rule.

sentences.zh: 又國朝沿唐制，以太尉掌誓戒。

translations.literal: The dynasty followed Tang practice: the Grand Marshal oversaw the abstention vows.
translations.idiomatic: The court kept the Tang arrangement—the Grand Marshal presided over the abstention vows.

sentences.zh: 今議太尉三公，非其所任，請以吏部尚書掌誓戒。

translations.literal: Now it was argued that the Grand Marshal, being one of the Three Ducal posts, was not suited to the duty; they requested that the Director of the Ministry of Personnel oversee the vows.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said the Grand Marshal, a nominal Three Ducal title, was wrong for the role and asked that the Minister of Personnel take charge of the vows.

sentences.zh: 詔用左僕射，闕則用右僕射、刑部尚書一員蒞之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered use of the Left Vice Director; if that post was vacant, one Right Vice Director or the Minister of Justice would attend.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered the Left Vice Director to preside; if absent, a Right Vice Director or the Minister of Justice would fill in.

sentences.zh: 熙寧四年，參知政事王珪言：「南郊，乘輿所過，必勘箭然後出入，此師行之法，不可施於郊祀。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xining, Vice Grand Councilor Wang Gui said: “At the southern suburban altar, wherever the imperial carriage passes, tally-arrows must be inspected before entry or exit—this is the method of army marches and must not be applied to suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In Xining 4, Vice Grand Councilor Wang Gui argued: “On the southern suburban progress every gate required tally-arrows before the imperial carriage could pass—an army field drill, unfit for suburban worship.

sentences.zh: 」禮院亦言。

translations.literal: ” The Ritual Office said the same.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Ritual Office agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是，凡車駕出入門皆罷之。

translations.literal: Thereupon all inspection of the imperial carriage at gates was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Every gate check on the imperial progress was abolished.

sentences.zh: 六年，以詳定所請，又罷太廟及宣德、朱雀、南薰諸門勘契。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, at the detailed regulations office’s request, tally verification at the Grand Ancestral Temple and at Xuande, Zhuque, and Nanxun gates was also abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In year six the review office won abolition of tally checks at the Grand Ancestral Temple and at Xuande, Zhuque, and Nanxun gates as well.

sentences.zh: 又皇帝自大次至版位，內臣二人執翟羽前導，號曰「拂翟」，失禮尤甚，請除之。

translations.literal: Also, when the emperor went from the inner rest pavilion to the ritual position, two inner attendants carrying pheasant feathers marched ahead as guides—a practice called “brushing the pheasant,” grossly contrary to ritual; it was requested that this be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Two inner attendants also marched ahead with pheasant plumes from the rest pavilion to the ritual stance—the “brushing the pheasant” parade, a grave breach; they asked that it be dropped.

sentences.zh: 凡郊壇，值雨雪，即齋宮門望祭殿望拜，祭日不設登歌，祀官以公服行事，中祀以上皆給明衣。

translations.literal: Whenever at the suburban altar there was rain or snow, they bowed from the fasting palace gate toward the hall of sacrifice; on the sacrifice day the ascent hymn was not installed; sacrifice officials acted in court dress; for medium sacrifices and above, bright robes were issued.
translations.idiomatic: Rain or snow at the suburban altar meant bowing from the fasting palace gate toward the sacrifice hall, no ascent hymn on the day itself, officials in court dress, and bright robes for medium rites and above.

sentences.zh: 開寶元年十一月郊，以燎壇稍遠，不聞告燎之聲，始用爟火，令光明遠照，通於祀所。

translations.literal: In the eleventh-month suburban rite of Kaibao 1, because the pyre altar stood somewhat far and the announce-the-blaze call could not be heard, they first used a signal fire so light would shine far and reach the sacrifice site.
translations.idiomatic: Kaibao 1’s eleventh-month suburban rite: the pyre stood too far to hear the blaze announcement, so they lit a beacon fire to carry light to the altar.

sentences.zh: 又太廟初獻，依開寶例，以玉斝、玉瓚，亞獻以金斝，終獻以瓢斝。

translations.literal: Also for the Grand Ancestral Temple first libation, following Kaibao precedent: jade goblet and jade libation cup; second libation, gold goblet; final libation, gourd goblet.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Ancestral Temple first offerings followed Kaibao: jade goblet and jade libation cup, gold for the second libation, gourd for the last.

sentences.zh: 外壇器亦如之。

translations.literal: Vessels at the outer altar were the same.
translations.idiomatic: The outer altar used the same vessels.

sentences.zh: 慶曆中，太常請皇帝獻天地、配帝以匏爵，亞獻以木爵。

translations.literal: In the Qingli era, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices requested that the emperor’s libation to Heaven and Earth and accompanying deities use gourd cups and the second libation use wood cups.
translations.idiomatic: During Qingli the Court of Imperial Sacrifices asked that Heaven, Earth, and accompanying deities receive gourd cups from the emperor and wood cups at the second libation.

sentences.zh: 親祠太廟，酌以玉斝，亞獻以金斝。

translations.literal: When the emperor personally sacrificed at the Grand Ancestral Temple, he ladled with a jade goblet; the second libation used a gold goblet.
translations.idiomatic: At personal Grand Ancestral Temple rites the emperor poured with a jade goblet; the second libation used gold.

sentences.zh: 郊廟飲福，皇帝皆以玉斝。

translations.literal: At suburban and temple blessing-wine drinking, the emperor always used jade goblets.
translations.idiomatic: For blessing wine at suburban and temple rites the emperor always drank from jade goblets.

sentences.zh: 詔飲福，唯用金斝。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that for blessing-wine drinking, only gold goblets be used.
translations.idiomatic: An edict limited blessing wine to gold goblets alone.

sentences.zh: 亞、終獻，酌以銀斝。

translations.literal: Second and final libations: ladle with silver goblets.
translations.idiomatic: Second and final libations were poured from silver goblets.

sentences.zh: 至飲福，尚食奉禦酌上尊酒，投溫器以進。

translations.literal: At blessing-wine drinking, the Imperial Kitchen Service had the imperial stewards ladle superior wine, warm it in a vessel, and present it.
translations.idiomatic: For blessing wine the Imperial Kitchen had stewards ladle top-grade wine, warm it, and serve it up.

sentences.zh: 凡常祀，天地宗廟，皆內降禦封香，仍制漆匱，付光祿、司農寺。

translations.literal: For routine sacrifices to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples, palace-sealed incense was always sent down, lacquer cases made, and the charge given to the Court of Imperial Entertainments and the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Routine Heaven, Earth, and temple rites always received palace-sealed incense in lacquer cases, handled by the Court of Imperial Entertainments and the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 每祠祭，命判寺官緘署禮料送祀所。

translations.literal: Each sacrifice, the officiating director was ordered to seal the ritual supplies and send them to the sacrifice site.
translations.idiomatic: Before each rite the presiding director sealed the ritual stores and forwarded them to the altar.

sentences.zh: 凡祈告，亦內出香。

translations.literal: For all prayer-announcements, incense also came from within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Prayer-announcements likewise drew incense from the palace.

sentences.zh: 遂為定制。

translations.literal: This became fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The practice became permanent law.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐中，裴煜請：「大祠悉降禦封香，中、小祠供太府香。

translations.literal: In the Jiayou era, Pei Yu requested: “Great sacrifices shall all receive palace-sealed incense; medium and small sacrifices shall be supplied with Grand Storehouse incense.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiayou, Pei Yu proposed: “Every great rite should get palace-sealed incense; medium and small rites should use Grand Storehouse incense.

sentences.zh: 中祠減大祠之半，小祠減中祠之半。

translations.literal: Medium sacrifices shall be half the great-sacrifice amount; small sacrifices half the medium amount.
translations.idiomatic: Medium rites would take half a great rite’s allotment; small rites half a medium rite’s.

sentences.zh: 東、西太一宮系大祠，歲太府供香，非時祈請，降禦封香准大祠例。

translations.literal: The Eastern and Western Great One Palaces count as great sacrifices; each year the Grand Storehouse supplies incense; off-schedule prayer requests receive palace-sealed incense on the great-sacrifice model.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern and Western Great One Palaces ranked as great rites—the Grand Storehouse supplied their yearly incense, while ad hoc prayers received palace-sealed incense as at a great rite.

sentences.zh: 及皇地祇、五方帝、百神、文宣、武成從配神位，牲牢寡薄。

translations.literal: Also at the cult positions of Earth Supreme, the Five Directional Emperors, the Hundred Spirits, and Wen Xuan and Wu Cheng as accompanying spirits, offerings of victims were meager and thin.
translations.idiomatic: Victims for Earth Supreme, the Five Directional Emperors, the Hundred Spirits, and Wen Xuan and Wu Cheng in accompanying seats were likewise too scant.

sentences.zh: 」呂公著亦論廟牲未備，悉加其數。

translations.literal: ” Lü Gongzhu also argued that temple victims were insufficient and all counts were increased.
translations.idiomatic: ” Lü Gongzhu too said temple victims fell short, and every quota was raised.

sentences.zh: 元符元年，左司員外郎曾旼言：「周人以氣臭事神，近世易之以香。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanfu, Left Office outsider Zeng Min said: “The Zhou used odor to serve the spirits; recent ages changed this to incense.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfu 1: Left Office outsider Zeng Min noted: “Zhou worship relied on smell; later ages switched to incense.

sentences.zh: 按何佟之議，以為南郊、明堂用沉香，本天之質，陽所宜也；

translations.literal: According to He Tongzhi’s argument, agarwood should be used at the southern suburb and Bright Hall—this is heaven’s substance, what yang should use;
translations.idiomatic: He Tongzhi had argued that agarwood suits the southern suburb and Bright Hall—heaven’s own quality, fit for yang;

sentences.zh: 北效用上和香，以地於人親，宜加雜馥。

translations.literal: the northern suburban altar should use supreme-harmony incense—earth is close kin to humans and should receive blended fragrances.
translations.idiomatic: the northern altar should use supreme-harmony incense—earth is kin to humanity and deserves mixed perfumes.

sentences.zh: 今令文北極天皇而下皆用濕香，至於眾星之位，香不復設，恐於義未盡。

translations.literal: Now the statutes use moist incense for the North Pole Heavenly Sovereign and below, yet at the star seats incense is no longer provided—perhaps the meaning is not fully expressed.
translations.idiomatic: Statutes today use moist incense down from the North Pole Heavenly Sovereign, yet star thrones go without incense—the symbolism may be incomplete.

sentences.zh: 」於是每陛各設香。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon incense was set at each terrace tier.
translations.idiomatic: ” Incense was placed on every terrace step.

sentences.zh: 又言：「先儒以為實柴所祀者無玉，郐鍮燎所祀者無幣。

translations.literal: He also said: “Earlier scholars held that the bao chai rite had no jade for what it worshipped, and the Kui and Tang blaze rites had no silk for what they worshipped.
translations.idiomatic: He added: “Old commentators said bao chai worship used no jade and Kui/Tang blaze worship used no silk.

sentences.zh: 今太常令式，眾星皆不用幣，蓋出於此。

translations.literal: Now in Court of Imperial Sacrifices regulations the stars all use no silk—probably from this.
translations.idiomatic: Current Court of Imperial Sacrifices forms withhold silk from all stars—likely from that reading.

sentences.zh: 然考《典瑞》、《玉人》之官，皆曰'圭璧以祀日月星辰'。

translations.literal: Yet examining the Directors of Regalia and Jade Workers, all say ‘gui and bi to sacrifice to sun, moon, stars, and constellations.’
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Directors of Regalia and Jade Workers both read: ‘gui and bi for sun, moon, stars, and constellations.’

sentences.zh: 則實柴所祀非無玉矣。

translations.literal: Then the bao chai sacrifice was not without jade.
translations.idiomatic: So bao chai was not jadeless after all.

sentences.zh: 郐鍮燎無幣，恐或未然。

translations.literal: That Kui and Tang blaze had no silk—perhaps that was not so.
translations.idiomatic: Whether Kui and Tang blaze truly lacked silk may be doubtful.

sentences.zh: 」至是遂命眾星隨其方色用幣。

translations.literal: ” At this time it was ordered that the stars use silk according to their directional colors.
translations.idiomatic: ” Stars were then ordered to use silk matching their directional colors.

sentences.zh: 慶曆三年，禮官余靖言：「祈穀、祀感生帝同日，其禮當異，不可皆用四圭有邸，色尚赤。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qingli, ritual official Yu Jing said: “Prayer for grain and sacrifice to the Life-Giving Emperor fall on the same day; their rites should differ—one cannot use for all the four-gui-with-base, color favoring red.
translations.idiomatic: Qingli 3: ritual officer Yu Jing said: “Prayer-for-grain and the Life-Giving Emperor share a day but not the same ritual—one cannot give every rite the four-gui-with-base in red.

sentences.zh: 」乃定祈穀、明堂蒼璧尺二寸，感生帝四圭有邸，朝日日圭、夕月月圭皆五寸，從祀神州無玉，報社稷兩圭有邸，祈不用玉。

translations.literal: ” They fixed: prayer-for-grain and Bright Hall, azure bi one foot two inches; Life-Giving Emperor, four gui with base; morning sun, sun gui, and evening moon, moon gui, both five inches; accompanying sacrifice to the Divine State, no jade; reporting to the altars of soil and grain, pair of gui with base; prayer, no jade.
translations.idiomatic: ” They set prayer-for-grain and Bright Hall at an azure bi of one foot two inches; Life-Giving Emperor at four gui with base; morning sun and evening moon gui at five inches each; Divine State accompaniment without jade; soil-and-grain reports with paired gui-with-base; prayers without jade.

sentences.zh: 明年，《祀儀》成，比《通禮》多所更定雲。

translations.literal: The next year the Sacrifice Regulament was completed, with many points revised against the Comprehensive Ritual, as recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Next year the Sacrifice Regulament appeared, revising much against the Comprehensive Ritual, as noted.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐中，集賢校理江休復言：「《六典》大祀養牲，在滌三月，袷享日近，已逾其期，而牲牢未供。

translations.literal: In Jiayou, Hanlin collator Jiang Xiufu said: “The Six Offices: great-sacrifice victims are kept in the cleansing pen three months; when the joint-honor day is near, the term is already passed yet victims are not supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayou: Hanlin collator Jiang Xiufu wrote: “The Six Offices require three months in the cleansing pen for great-sacrifice beasts—yet joint-honor day nears past deadline with victims still missing.

sentences.zh: 乞依漢、唐置廩犧局。

translations.literal: Request establishing a grain-and-victim bureau per Han and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for a grain-and-victim bureau on Han and Tang models.

sentences.zh: 」下禮院議：歲大小祀幾百數，而牲盛之事，儲養無素，宜如休復言。

translations.literal: ” Referred to the Ritual Office: each year large and small sacrifices number in the hundreds, yet storing and raising victims lacks standing provision—it should follow Xiufu’s proposal.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Ritual Office replied: hundreds of rites yearly, yet no standing herd—Xiufu’s plan should be adopted.

sentences.zh: 乃置廩犧局，設牢預養，籍田舊地，種植粢盛，納於神倉，以待祭祀之用。

translations.literal: Thereupon they established the Grain-and-Victim Bureau, set up pens for advance raising, used the old register-field land to plant offering grain, stored it in the god granary, and awaited sacrifice use.
translations.idiomatic: They then founded the Grain-and-Victim Bureau, pre-raised stock in pens, planted offering grain on old register fields, and filled the god granary for rites to come.

sentences.zh: 元豐六年，詳定禮文所言：「本朝昊天上帝、皇地祇、太祖位各設三牲，非尚質貴誠之義。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanfeng, the detailed ritual text office said: “Our dynasty sets three victims each at Supreme Heaven, Earth Supreme, and Taizu’s positions—this is not the principle of valuing simplicity and honoring sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfeng 6: the ritual review office said: “Three victims each at Supreme Heaven, Earth Supreme, and Taizu’s seats betray simplicity and sincerity.

sentences.zh: 請親祠圜丘、方澤正配位皆用犢，不設羊豕俎及鼎匕，有司攝事亦如之。

translations.literal: Request that personal sacrifice at the Round Altars and Square Mound primary and accompanying positions all use calves alone, without sheep and pig trays or tripod ladles; officials standing in likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Personal rites at Round Altar and Square Mound, primary and accompanying, should use calves only—no sheep or pig trays or tripod ladles; proxies the same.

sentences.zh: 又簠、簋、尊、豆皆非陶器，及用龍杓。

translations.literal: Also the grain and meat vessels, wine jars, and offering bowls are all not pottery, and they use dragon ladles.
translations.idiomatic: Grain vessels, wine jars, and offering bowls were not pottery; dragon ladles were used.

sentences.zh: 請改用陶，以椫為杓。

translations.literal: Request changing to pottery and using birch for ladles.
translations.idiomatic: They asked for pottery ware and birch ladles.

sentences.zh: 又請南北郊先行升煙瘞血之禮，至薦奠畢，即如舊儀，於壇坎燔瘞牲幣。

translations.literal: Also request that at southern and northern suburbs the rites of ascending smoke and burying blood be performed first; when offering is complete, follow the old rite of burning and burying victims and silk in altar pits.
translations.idiomatic: They also wanted southern and northern suburbs to open with smoke ascent and blood burial, then after offerings finish burn and bury victims and silk in the pits as before.

sentences.zh: 又北郊皇地祇及神州地祇，當為坎瘞，今乃建壇燔燎，非是。

translations.literal: Also, for northern suburb Earth Supreme and Divine State Earth Spirit, there should be pit burial; now they build altars and burn—this is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Northern rites to Earth Supreme and the Divine State Earth Spirit should bury in pits, not burn on built altars—that was the error.

sentences.zh: 請今祭地祝版、牲幣並瘞於坎。

translations.literal: Request that henceforth earth-sacrifice prayer boards, victims, and silk all be buried in the pit.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth prayer boards, victims, and silk at earth rites should all go into the pit.

sentences.zh: 又《祀儀》：惟昊天上帝、皇地祇、高禖燔瘞犢首，自感生帝、神州地祇而下皆不燔瘞牲體，殊不應典禮。

translations.literal: Also the Sacrifice Regulament: only Supreme Heaven, Earth Supreme, and High Consort burn and bury calf heads; from Life-Giving Emperor and Divine State Earth Spirit downward none burn or bury victim flesh—greatly not matching canonical rite.
translations.idiomatic: The Sacrifice Regulament burned and buried calf heads only for Supreme Heaven, Earth Supreme, and High Consort; below Life-Giving Emperor and Divine State Earth Spirit no flesh was burned or buried—a wide miss against the classics.

sentences.zh: 請自今昊天上帝、感生帝皆燔牲首以報陽；

translations.literal: Request that from now Supreme Heaven and Life-Giving Emperor all burn victim heads to report yang;
translations.idiomatic: They asked that Supreme Heaven and Life-Giving Emperor hereafter burn victim heads to answer yang;

sentences.zh: 皇地祇、神州、太社、太稷，凡地之祭，皆瘞牲之左髀以報陰。

translations.literal: Earth Supreme, Divine State, Grand Soil and Grain altars—for all earth sacrifices, bury the victim’s left shank to report yin.
translations.idiomatic: Earth Supreme, Divine State, and the Grand Soil and Grain altars—all earth rites should bury the victim’s left shank for yin.

sentences.zh: 薦享太廟亦皆升首於室。」

translations.literal: Grand Ancestral Temple offerings likewise all raise heads to the inner chamber.”
translations.idiomatic: Grand Ancestral Temple offerings should likewise raise heads to the inner chamber.”

sentences.zh: 又言：「古者祭祀用牲，有豚解，有體解，薦腥則解為十一體。

translations.literal: He also said: “Anciently sacrifice victims had whole-pig dismemberment and body dismemberment; for presenting raw meat they dismembered into eleven parts.
translations.idiomatic: He went on: “Ancient victims were cut whole-pig style or body style; raw offerings came in eleven pieces.

sentences.zh: 今親祠南郊，正配位之俎，不殊左右胖，不分貴賤，無豚解、體解之別。

translations.literal: Now at personal southern-suburb sacrifice, the primary and accompanying trays do not distinguish left and right sides, do not separate noble and common, and have no distinction of whole-pig or body dismemberment.
translations.idiomatic: Today’s personal southern suburb makes no left-right split on primary and accompanying trays, no rank distinction, no whole-pig versus body cut.

sentences.zh: 請郊廟薦腥，解其牲兩髀、兩肩、兩肋並脊為七體，左右胖俱用。

translations.literal: Request that suburban and temple raw presentation dismember the victim’s two thighs, two shoulders, two ribs, and spine into seven parts; both left and right sides used.
translations.idiomatic: Suburban and temple raw offerings should split two thighs, two shoulders, two ribs, and the spine into seven parts, using both sides.

sentences.zh: 其載於俎，以兩髀在端，兩肩、兩肋次之，脊居中，皆進末。

translations.literal: Loaded on the tray: both thighs at the ends, shoulders and ribs next, spine centered, all presented end-first.
translations.idiomatic: On the tray both thighs go to the ends, shoulders and ribs follow, spine in the middle, each piece presented end-first.

sentences.zh: 至薦熟，沉肉于湯，止用右胖。

translations.literal: When presenting cooked meat, meat is steeped in broth; only the right side is used.
translations.idiomatic: Cooked offerings steep the meat in broth and use only the right side.

sentences.zh: 髀不升俎，前後肱骨離為三，曰肩、臂、臑。

translations.literal: Thighs do not ascend the tray; front and rear arm bones are separated into three, called shoulder, arm, and shank.
translations.idiomatic: Thighs never mount the tray; fore and hind arm bones divide into shoulder, arm, and shank.

sentences.zh: 後髀股骨去體離為二，曰肫、胳。

translations.literal: The rear thigh, with thigh bone removed from the body, is split into two, called shin and flank.
translations.idiomatic: The hind quarter, thigh bone stripped from the carcass, yields shin and flank.

sentences.zh: 前脊謂之正脊，次直謂之脡脊，闊於脡脊謂之橫脊，皆二骨。

translations.literal: The front spine is called the proper spine; the next straight section the filet spine; wider than the filet, the cross spine—all of two bones.
translations.idiomatic: The fore spine is the proper spine; the next straight strip the filet spine; broader still, the cross spine—each of two bones.

sentences.zh: 肋骨最後二為短肋，旁中二為正肋，最前二為代肋。

translations.literal: Of the ribs, the last two are short ribs, the middle two at the sides are proper ribs, and the foremost two are substitute ribs.
translations.idiomatic: Ribs count from the rear: last pair short ribs, middle pair proper ribs, front pair substitute ribs.

sentences.zh: 若升俎，則肩、臂臑在上端，膊、胳在下端，脊、肋在中央。

translations.literal: If ascending the tray, shoulder, arm, and shank go at the upper end; flank and shin at the lower end; spine and ribs in the center.
translations.idiomatic: On the tray shoulder, arm, and shank sit uppermost; flank and shin below; spine and ribs in the center.

sentences.zh: 其俎之序，則肩、臂、臑、正脊、脡脊、橫脊、代肋、長肋、短肋、膊、胳凡十一體，而骨體升俎，進神坐前如少牢禮，皆進下。

translations.literal: The tray order: shoulder, arm, shank, proper spine, filet spine, cross spine, substitute rib, long ribs, short ribs, flank, shin—eleven parts in all; bones and flesh ascending the tray before the spirit seat as in the lesser pen rite, all presented bottom-first.
translations.idiomatic: Order runs shoulder, arm, shank, proper spine, filet spine, cross spine, substitute rib, long ribs, short ribs, flank, shin—eleven pieces; like the lesser pen rite before the spirit seat, all presented bottom-first.

sentences.zh: 其牲體各預以半為腥俎，半為熟俎，腸胃膚俎亦然。」

translations.literal: Each victim body is beforehand half for the raw tray, half for the cooked tray; intestinal, stomach, and skin trays are likewise.”
translations.idiomatic: Each carcass is split beforehand: half raw tray, half cooked; intestinal, stomach, and skin trays follow the same rule.”

sentences.zh: 又請：「親祠飲福酒訖，仿《儀禮》'佐食摶黍'之說，命太官令取忝於簋，摶以授祝，祝受以豆，以嘏乎皇帝而無嘏辭。

translations.literal: He also requested: “After the emperor drinks blessing wine at personal sacrifice, following the Ceremonial Rites ‘associate presents millet’ account, order the Grand Kitchen Director to take millet from the grain vessel, knead it, and give it to the invocator; the invocator receives it in a bowl and offers blessing to the emperor without blessing words.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked: “After the emperor’s blessing wine at a personal rite, echoing the Ceremonial Rites ‘associate kneads millet,’ the Grand Kitchen Director should take millet from the grain vessel, knead it, hand it to the invocator, who receives it in a bowl and blesses the emperor—without a spoken blessing.

sentences.zh: 又本朝親祠南郊，習儀於壇所，明堂習儀於大慶殿，皆近於瀆。

translations.literal: Also, for our dynasty’s personal southern-suburb sacrifice, rehearsal is at the altar site; Bright Hall rehearsal is at Great Celebration Hall—both too close and profane.
translations.idiomatic: Personal southern-suburb rehearsals at the altar itself and Bright Hall drills in Great Celebration Hall both hug the spirits too closely—near profanation.

sentences.zh: 伏請南郊習儀於青城，明堂習儀於尚書省，以遠神為恭。

translations.literal: Humbly request southern-suburb rehearsal at Qingcheng and Bright Hall rehearsal at the Masters of Writing headquarters, taking distance from the spirits as reverence.
translations.idiomatic: They pleaded to rehearse southern rites at Qingcheng and Bright Hall rites at the Masters of Writing compound—distance as reverence.

sentences.zh: 又賜胙：三師，三公，侍中，中書令，門下、中書侍郎，尚書左、右丞，知樞密、同知院事，禮儀、儀仗、鹵簿、頓遞使，牛羊豕肩、臂、臑各五；

translations.literal: Also sacrificial meat grants: Three Preceptors, Three Ducal ministers, Palace Attendants, Grand Secretariat Directors, Vice Directors of the Gate and Secretariat, Left and Right Masters of Writing Vice Directors, heads of Military Affairs, ritual protocol, honor, halberd, and relay commissioners—ox, sheep, and pig shoulder, arm, and shank, five each;
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial meat went to the Three Preceptors, Three Ducal ministers, Palace Attendants, Secretariat chiefs, Gate and Secretariat vice ministers, Masters of Writing deputies, Military Affairs heads, and the ritual, honor, halberd, and relay commissioners—five each of ox, sheep, and pig shoulder, arm, and shank;

sentences.zh: 太子三師、三少，特進，觀文大學士、學士，御史大夫，六尚書，金紫、銀青光祿大夫，節度使，資政殿大學士，觀文翰林資政端明龍圖天章寶文承旨、侍講、侍讀，學士，左右散騎常侍，尚書列曹侍郎，龍圖、天章、寶文直學士，光祿、正議、通議大夫，御史中丞，太子賓客、詹事，給事中，中書舍人，節度觀察留後，左右諫議，龍圖、天章、寶文待制，太中、中大夫，秘書、殿中丞，太常、宗正卿，牛豕肩、臂、臑各三；

translations.literal: Crown Prince Three Preceptors and Three Junior Tutors, Special Advancement holders, Exalted Culture grand and regular academicians, censor-in-chief, the six ministers, gold- and silver-purple Grand Masters for Splendid Happiness, military commissioners, Palatial Hall grand academicians, Exalted Culture, Hanlin, Palatial Hall, Brightly Lit, Dragon Hall, Heavenly Chapter, and Precious Literature chancellors, lecturers and readers, academicians, Left and Right Regular Attendants, Masters of Writing bureau vice ministers, Dragon Hall, Heavenly Chapter, and Precious Literature direct academicians, Court of Imperial Entertainments, Correct and Universal grand masters, vice censor-in-chief, Crown Prince guests of honor and household heads, recipients of edicts, Secretariat drafters, military observation and acting commissioners, Left and Right Remonstrators, Dragon Hall, Heavenly Chapter, and Precious Literature awaiting appointment, Grand and Regular grand masters, Secretariat and Palace director deputies, Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Imperial Clan directors—ox and pig shoulder, arm, and shank, three each;
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince’s tutors, Special Advancement holders, Exalted Culture and Hanlin academicians, censor-in-chief, six ministers, gold- and silver-purple grand masters, commissioners, Palatial Hall scholars, lecturers and readers, Regular Attendants, bureau vice ministers, direct academicians, Court of Imperial Entertainments and Correct and Universal grand masters, vice censor-in-chief, Crown Prince staff, edict recipients, drafters, observation commissioners, remonstrators, awaiting-appointment scholars, grand masters, director deputies, and Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Imperial Clan chiefs received three each of ox and pig shoulder, arm, and shank;

sentences.zh: 入內內侍省押班、副都知，光祿卿，監禮官，博士，牛羊脊、肋各三；

translations.literal: Inner Service deputy directors and deputy heads, Court of Imperial Entertainments director, supervising ritual officials, erudites—ox and sheep spine and ribs, three each;
translations.idiomatic: Inner Service deputies, the Court of Imperial Entertainments director, ritual supervisors, and erudites received three each of ox and sheep spine and ribs;

sentences.zh: 太祝，奉禮，司奠彝，郊社、太廟、宮闈令，監牲牢、供應祠事內官，羊髀、膊、胳三；

translations.literal: Grand invocator, ritual attendants, vessel officers, suburban and temple directors, and inner attendants supervising victims and supply—sheep thigh, flank, and shin, three;
translations.idiomatic: Grand invocators, ritual attendants, vessel officers, suburban and temple directors, and inner attendants overseeing victims and supplies received three of sheep thigh, flank, and shin;

sentences.zh: 應執事、職掌、樂工、門幹、宰手、馭馬、馭車人，並均給脾、肫、胳、觳及腸、胃、膚之類。」

translations.literal: All who perform duties, clerks, musicians, gate guards, butchers, horse and cart drivers—equally given spleen, shin, flank, bones, and intestine, stomach, skin, and the like.”
translations.idiomatic: Every functionary, clerk, musician, gate guard, butcher, and driver shared alike in spleen, shin, flank, bones, intestines, stomach, skin, and the rest.”
